gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's maker-store prices for the single-unit 120/240 V stations. Checked on 2026-11-17, the BLUETTI Apex 300 is the cheapest at $1,499 (list $1,699). The Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus is $3,499 but sold out, with pre-orders shipping Dec 2. The EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra listing is $3,699 and the DELTA Pro Ultra X is $7,899. Anker's own page for the F3800 Plus, the mid-range pick ChatGPT priced at $2,999.99, shows 'Sold Out' and no price.
standout_why: Cited rivals compared: Watt & Warden (wattandwarden.com split-phase page) and Power Station Field Guide (powerstationpilot.com/needs/240v-split-phase). Watt & Warden gives one dated price, F3800 Plus at $3,199.99 'as of November 16, 2026', and shows 'Check price' for the DELTA Pro Ultra, Apex 300 and DELTA Pro 3. Power Station Field Guide lists no prices. Neither gives prices for the Jackery 5000 Plus or DELTA Pro Ultra X, says the 5000 Plus is on pre-order, says the F3800 Plus is sold out on Anker's store, or works out cost per kWh across the single-unit set. Watt & Warden already covers the per-leg limits: Apex 300 about two 1,920 W legs, and 6,000 W combined (not per leg) on the F3800 Plus. That point is not new.
decides: On price it confirms the Apex 300 as the entry pick for single-unit 240 V: $1,499 and $542 per kWh, the lowest from a maker store today. Its catch is 3,840 W combined, about 1,920 W per leg according to Watt & Warden, so it can't run a 20 A, 4,800 W 240 V load. For bigger loads, the cheapest maker-store option you can buy today is the DELTA Pro Ultra listing at $3,699 (7,200 W, 6,144 Wh, about $602 per kWh). The Jackery 5000 Plus costs less ($3,499) but is pre-order only until Dec 2. ChatGPT's F3800 Plus pick at $2,999.99 can't be verified on Anker's store today.
